p.stmt: Prove: if lim_{x->a} f(x) = L and lim_{x->a} g(x) = M then lim_{x->a} (f(x)+g(x)) = L+M

w:
Let epsilon > 0. Since f -> L there is delta1 with |f(x)-L| < epsilon/2 when 0<|x-a|<delta1.
Since g -> M there is delta2 with |g(x)-M| < epsilon/2 when 0<|x-a|<delta2.
Let delta = min(delta1, delta2) and suppose 0<|x-a|<delta.
Then |f(x)+g(x)-(L+M)| <= |f(x)-L| + |g(x)-M| < epsilon/2 + epsilon/2 = epsilon.
why: standard epsilon/2 argument via triangle inequality
